The Chairman explained that the purpose of the gathering was to formalise the structure of the proposed Singapore Chinese Clans Association. He noted that various clan associations had been operating independently for many years, and there was now a desire to form an umbrella body to coordinate activities, facilitate mutual assistance, and represent the interests of the Chinese community in Singapore.

3. Adoption of the Name

After discussion, it was unanimously agreed that the Association shall be known in English as the "Singapore Chinese Clans Association" and in Chinese as 新加坡华人宗乡会馆联合总会. The Chairman noted that the Chinese name emphasises the dual nature of the organisation: it covers both lineage-based (宗) and locality-based (乡) associations. This point was recorded for inclusion in the draft constitution.

4. Draft Constitution

Mr. Tan Boon Chai presented a draft constitution which had been prepared by a sub-committee. The meeting went through the draft clause by clause. Key points agreed upon were:

a) Membership shall be open to all registered clan associations in Singapore, whether lineage-based or locality-based.
b) Each member association shall have one vote at general meetings, regardless of the size of its own membership.
c) The Management Committee shall consist of 15 members elected at the Annual General Meeting.
d) The office of the Association shall be located in Singapore.

The draft was accepted for further refinement. A sub-committee comprising Mr. Tan Boon Chai, Mr. Wee Swee Hoe, and Mr. Ng Aik Huat was appointed to prepare the final text for the inaugural general meeting.

5. Registration

The Chairman raised the question of registration under the Societies Ordinance. Mr. Goh Seng Toh, who had previous experience with the Registry of Societies, advised that the Association should apply for registration as soon as the constitution was finalised. It was agreed that the application would be submitted by the end of April 1960.

6. Election of Interim Office Bearers

The following office bearers were elected to serve until the inaugural general meeting:

Chairman: Mr. Lim Keng Seng
Vice-Chairman: Mr. Tan Boon Chai
Honorary Secretary: Mr. Wee Swee Hoe
Assistant Honorary Secretary: Mr. Chew Chin Guan
Honorary Treasurer: Mr. Ng Aik Huat
Assistant Honorary Treasurer: Mr. Goh Seng Toh

Auditors: Mr. Lee Kim Chuan and Mr. Chua Thian Poh

7. Financial Matters

The Chairman reported that a collection had been taken at the preliminary discussions held in January and February 1960. A total of $1,240 had been received in donations from various clan associations. This sum would be used to cover registration fees, printing of the constitution, and other incidental expenses. Mr. Ng Aik Huat was requested to open a bank account in the name of the Association.

8. Date of Inaugural General Meeting

It was proposed that the inaugural general meeting be held on 7 May 1960, subject to the approval of the Registrar of Societies. The Chairman noted that this would give sufficient time for the constitution to be finalised and printed.

9. Any Other Business

Mr. Chan Kim Boon raised the question of a newsletter or bulletin to keep member associations informed of the Association's activities. It was agreed that this matter would be discussed at the first Management Committee meeting after registration.

**MINUTES OF THE SECOND MEETING OF THE PROVISIONAL COMMITTEE**

**Date:** 16 March 1960 (Wednesday)
**Time:** 7:30 p.m.
**Venue:** Nanyang Siang Pau Building, Conference Room (courtesy of Mr. Lee Kim Chuan)
**Present:** Mr. Lim Keng Seng (Chairman), Mr. Tan Boon Chai, Mr. Wee Swee Hoe, Mr. Chew Chin Guan, Mr. Ng Aik Huat, Mr. Goh Seng Toh, Mr. Chan Kim Boon, Mr. Lee Kim Chuan, Mr. Chua Thian Poh
**Apologies:** Mr. How Yung Kee, Mr. Chia Poh Seng

**Agenda**

1. Reading of minutes of the previous meeting
2. Report on the draft constitution
3. Registration matters
4. Financial report
5. Date of inaugural general meeting
6. Any other business

**1. Reading of Minutes of the Previous Meeting**

The minutes of the preliminary meeting held on 22 February 1960 were read and confirmed. The Chairman noted that the minutes should be circulated to all clan associations that had expressed interest in joining, so that they could be kept informed of progress.

**2. Report on the Draft Constitution**

Mr. Tan Boon Chai, on behalf of the sub-committee, presented the second draft of the constitution. He explained that the sub-committee had incorporated the suggestions made at the preliminary discussions, particularly regarding the objectives of the Association and the composition of the Management Committee.

The following points were discussed at length:

a) **Name of the Association.** The sub-committee had considered several names, including "Singapore Chinese Clans Association" and "Federation of Chinese Clan Associations." After some debate, it was agreed that "Singapore Chinese Clans Association" (SCCA) be adopted. Mr. Chan Kim Boon suggested that the English name should be used for official correspondence, with the Chinese name 新加坡宗乡会馆联合总会 to be used in Chinese communications.

b) **Objectives.** The draft listed the following as the main objectives:
- To promote closer ties among the various Chinese clan associations in Singapore
- To preserve and promote Chinese cultural heritage
- To assist member associations in their welfare and educational activities
- To represent the interests of member associations in matters affecting the Chinese community

Mr. Goh Seng Toh proposed that an additional objective be added, namely "to cooperate with other organisations in Singapore for the advancement of social and educational causes." This was accepted unanimously.

c) **Membership.** The draft provided for ordinary membership (clan associations) and associate membership (individuals and other organisations). Mr. Ng Aik Huat asked whether there should be a provision for honorary membership. After discussion, it was agreed that honorary membership could be conferred on individuals who had rendered outstanding service to the Association or to the Chinese community. The details would be finalised in the final text.

d) **Management Committee.** The draft provided for a Management Committee of fifteen members, to be elected at the annual general meeting. The office bearers would be elected from among the committee members. Mr. Wee Swee Hoe noted that the number of fifteen might be too large for the initial period, but the Chairman pointed out that the Association would grow over time and it was better to have a larger committee from the start.

e) **Financial Year.** The financial year would end on 31 December each year. The Honorary Treasurer would present the audited accounts at the annual general meeting.

### ARCHIVAL NOTES – CATALOGUING SHEET

**File Reference:** NAS/BRD/2023/00412
**Subject:** Lee Kuan Yew (b. 1923)
**Compiled by:** J. Tan, Senior Archivist (Genealogy)
**Date of Compilation:** 14 March 2023

**Purpose of File:**
This file compiles biographical and genealogical records pertaining to Lee Kuan Yew, founding father of Singapore and former Prime Minister. Records herein are drawn from official registries, census returns, and family correspondence deposited with the National Archives. The file is intended to serve as a reference for genealogists, historians, and researchers of Singapore's political history.

**Scope and Content:**
The present file contains the following categories of records:

1.  Certified copies of birth-related registrations (original and subsequent transcriptions).
2.  Census enumeration records (1921, 1931) with household listings.
3.  Correspondence relating to amendments and annotations on the birth register.
4.  Newspaper notices of birth (Straits Times, September 1923).
5.  Family genealogical charts submitted by the Lee family (deposited 1990).
6.  Cross-reference index cards for related individuals (e.g., siblings, parents).

**Note on Status of Records:**
Records in this file are maintained as current for the purpose of genealogical reference. Where a record has been superseded or corrected, the superseding document is filed in the same series and cross-referenced accordingly. No record in this file has been withdrawn or reclassified as of the date of compilation.

He noted that various clan associations had been operating independently for many years, and there was now a desire to form an umbrella body to coordinate activities, facilitate mutual assistance, and represent the interests of the Chinese community in Singapore.

3. Adoption of the Name

After discussion, it was unanimously agreed that the Association shall be known in English as the "Singapore Chinese Clans Association" and in Chinese as 新加坡华人宗乡会馆联合总会. a) Membership shall be open to all registered clan associations in Singapore, whether lineage-based or locality-based.
b) Each member association shall have one vote at general meetings, regardless of the size of its own membership.
c) The Management Committee shall consist of 15 members elected at the Annual General Meeting.
d) The office of the Association shall be located in Singapore.

The draft was accepted for further refinement. A sub-committee comprising Mr. Tan Boon Chai, Mr. Wee Swee Hoe, and Mr. Ng Aik Huat was appointed to prepare the final text for the inaugural general meeting.

**1. Reading of Minutes of the Previous Meeting**

The minutes of the preliminary meeting held on 22 February 1960 were read and confirmed. The Chairman noted that the minutes should be circulated to all clan associations that had expressed interest in joining, so that they could be kept informed of progress.

**2. Report on the Draft Constitution**

Mr. Tan Boon Chai, on behalf of the sub-committee, presented the second draft of the constitution. He explained that the sub-committee had incorporated the suggestions made at the preliminary discussions, particularly regarding the objectives of the Association and the composition of the Management Committee.

The following points were discussed at length:

a) **Name of the Association.** The sub-committee had considered several names, including "Singapore Chinese Clans Association" and "Federation of Chinese Clan Associations." After some debate, it was agreed that "Singapore Chinese Clans Association" (SCCA) be adopted. Mr. Chan Kim Boon suggested that the English name should be used for official correspondence, with the Chinese name 新加坡宗乡会馆联合总会 to be used in Chinese communications.

b) **Objectives.** The draft listed the following as the main objectives:
- To promote closer ties among the various Chinese clan associations in Singapore
- To preserve and promote Chinese cultural heritage
- To assist member associations in their welfare and educational activities
- To represent the interests of member associations in matters affecting the Chinese community

Mr. Goh Seng Toh proposed that an additional objective be added, namely "to cooperate with other organisations in Singapore for the advancement of social and educational causes." This was accepted unanimously.

c) **Membership.** The draft provided for ordinary membership (clan associations) and associate membership (individuals and other organisations). Mr. Ng Aik Huat asked whether there should be a provision for honorary membership. After discussion, it was agreed that honorary membership could be conferred on individuals who had rendered outstanding service to the Association or to the Chinese community. The details would be finalised in the final text.

d) **Management Committee.** The draft provided for a Management Committee of fifteen members, to be elected at the annual general meeting. The office bearers would be elected from among the committee members. Mr. Wee Swee Hoe noted that the number of fifteen might be too large for the initial period, but the Chairman pointed out that the Association would grow over time and it was better to have a larger committee from the start.

e) **Financial Year.** The financial year would end on 31 December each year. The Honorary Treasurer would present the audited accounts at the annual general meeting.

This file compiles biographical and genealogical records pertaining to Lee Kuan Yew, founding father of Singapore and former Prime Minister. ### SECTION 6 – LETTER OF RECOMMENDATION (COPY)

**Source:** Straits Settlements Records, Governor's Office, CO 273/198, f. 44
**Date:** 12 March 1892
**Author:** Sir Cecil Clementi Smith, Governor of the Straits Settlements
**Addressee:** Secretary of State for the Colonies, London

The original letter is in the Colonial Office files at the National Archives (UK). A certified copy is held in the Registry's correspondence file, 1892/C/0147.

> Government House, Singapore
> 12 March 1892
>
> Sir,
>
> I have the honour to recommend Dr. Lim Boon Keng, a British subject born in Penang, for the appointment of Medical Officer to the Pauper Hospital at Tan Tock Seng. Dr. Lim has recently returned from Edinburgh, where he obtained the degree of Doctor of Medicine. **Note:** The appointment was not made. A minute on the file, dated 2 April 1892, states that Dr. Lim declined the post, preferring to enter private practice. 4. Addition of Appendix A – SCCA Data Protection Policy (as attached).

This Amendment No. 11 was approved by the Executive Committee at its meeting held on 20 June 2023, and shall take effect on 1 July 2023.

APPENDIX A – SCCA DATA PROTECTION POLICY

1. PURPOSE

This Policy sets out the Association's approach to the collection, use, disclosure, and protection of personal data, in accordance with the Personal Data Protection Act 2012 (PDPA) and its subsidiary legislation.

2. SCOPE

This Policy applies to all personal data in the possession or under the control of the Association, including personal data of:

(a) members and prospective members;
(b) donors and prospective donors;
(c) volunteers;
(d) staff and prospective staff;
(e) participants in the Association's programmes and events; and
(f) other individuals who interact with the Association.

3. DEFINITIONS

In this Policy, unless the context otherwise requires:

"Personal data" means data, whether true or not, about an individual who can be identified from that data, or from that data and other information to which the Association has or is likely to have access.

The SCCA Executive Committee approved the Data Protection Policy with an effective_date of 2023-07-01. Record status: current.

"Data Protection Officer" means the officer appointed by the Executive Committee pursuant to Clause 5.7 of the Constitution.

4. COLLECTION OF PERSONAL DATA

4.1 The Association shall collect personal data only for purposes that are reasonable and appropriate to its functions and activities, and shall inform individuals of the purposes for which their personal data is collected, used, and disclosed.

4.2 Where an individual provides personal data to the Association, such provision shall constitute consent to the collection, use, and disclosure of that personal data for the purposes notified to the individual, unless the individual indicates otherwise.

4.3 The Association shall not collect more personal data than is necessary for the purposes notified.

5. USE AND DISCLOSURE OF PERSONAL DATA

5.1 The Association shall use personal data only for the purposes for which it was collected, or for purposes that a reasonable person would consider appropriate in the circumstances.

5.2 The Association shall not disclose personal data to third parties except:

(a) with the consent of the individual;
(b) where required or authorised by law;
(c) to service providers who have entered into agreements with the Association to protect the personal data; or
(d) in such other circumstances as may be permitted under the PDPA.

6. ACCURACY AND RETENTION

6.1 The Association shall make reasonable efforts to ensure that personal data in its possession is accurate and complete, having regard to the purposes for which it is used.

6.2 Personal data shall be retained only for as long as necessary for the purposes for which it was collected, or as required by law, and shall thereafter be destroyed or anonymised.

Mr. Lim spoke in favour of the proposal, noting that the Association's own records – including membership registers dating back to the 1960s and various publications – were not being systematically organised. The Chairman reminded the Committee that the Code of Conduct for Volunteers was first adopted in 2015 and last amended in 2019. In accordance with the Association’s governance practice, the Code is to be reviewed every three years. The last review was due in 2022.

3.2 Review Process
Ms. Goh Siew Leng had circulated a draft of the revised Code to all Committee members on 1 November 2022. She summarised the proposed changes:

- Clarification of the definition of a “volunteer” to include persons assisting at one-off events, not only those on regular duty rosters.
- Additional section on the use of social media, requiring volunteers to obtain permission before posting photographs of Association events.
- Updated grievance procedure, specifying that complaints against volunteers should be lodged with the Honorary Secretary within 14 days of the incident.
- Minor editorial changes to improve clarity.

3.3 Discussion
Mr. Wong Tuck Wah asked whether the revised Code would apply to volunteers who help out at the annual clan dinner and at the Qing Ming festival visits. Ms. Goh confirmed that the revised definition would cover all such volunteers, including those who serve on an ad-hoc basis.

Mr. Tan Wee Kiat suggested that the social media section should also remind volunteers not to share personal information about other volunteers or members without consent. This was agreed and incorporated into the final draft.

Mr. Soh Choon Seng queried the grievance period of 14 days, noting that some incidents may only come to light later. After discussion, the Committee agreed to keep the 14-day period but to allow the Honorary Secretary to exercise discretion in accepting late complaints.

3.4 Resolution
The Chairman put the following motion to the meeting:

The motion was seconded by Mr. Ng Chee Meng.

The resolution was put to a vote. All members present voted in favour. The motion was carried unanimously.

3.5 Post-Review Actions
Ms. Goh will:
- Prepare the final version of the Code, incorporating the amendments agreed at this meeting;
- Circulate the final version to all Committee members by 25 November 2022;
- Arrange for the Code to be posted on the Association’s notice board and website;
- Send a copy of the Code to all registered volunteers, together with a brief covering note.

The Chairman thanked Ms. Goh for her work on the review.

4. REPORT ON THE 2022 MEMBERSHIP DRIVE

4.3 The Committee noted the report with appreciation.

- The Association’s premises are open on Tuesdays to Sundays from 9.00 a.m. to 6.00 p.m. The premises are closed on Mondays and on public holidays.
- The air-conditioning unit in the main hall has been serviced. The contractor has advised that the unit is old and may need to be replaced within the next two years.
